food_database_record_id: Results: organosulfur profiles in raw garlic; Table 1 control (75 °C, 0 min)
synonym_verification_status: Allicin was synthesized from diallyl disulfide, purified, identified by LC-APCI-MS/MS (92.0% purity) and included among the OSC reference standards.
mapping_review_rationale: Primary study reports the exact organosulfur analyte in raw garlic paste and identifies/quantifies with compound reference standards; exact Stage B target ID verified.
moisture_basis: Dry-weight basis as explicitly stated by source; paste was made from garlic cloves and water, and moisture was determined by freeze-drying. No fresh-weight conversion.
analytical_method: HPLC-UV at 254 nm on C18; LC-APCI-MS/MS used for identification of isolated OSCs. Source says individual compounds quantified with OSC reference standards.
extraction_method: 10 g garlic homogenate extracted with hexane (3 × 10 mL); combined organic extracts evaporated under air at room temperature; residue reconstituted in acetonitrile, filtered, HPLC analyzed.
sample_size: Three replicate sample preparations (source states all preparations in triplicate)
source_title: Effect of different combined mechanical and thermal treatments on the quality characteristics of garlic paste
extraction_notes: Reported raw-control mean 5.59 ± 0.26 mg/g dry weight; normalized arithmetically to 5590.0 mg/kg dry weight. Mean and SD transcribed without inferring unreported sample-level replicates. Table 1 labels 75°C/0 min treatment sequence groups; result narrative reports raw-garlic profile. Values retained at group mean level. Source reported 5.59 mg/g dry weight; arithmetically normalized ×1000 to mg/kg dry weight. The primary article explicitly states that all OSC concentrations are on a dry-weight basis and moisture was determined by freeze-drying.
uncertainty_notes: The garlic paste was prepared with 50 mL water per 100 g cloves, while concentrations are reported on dry-weight basis; source denominator linkage requires review. Three replicate preparations may be analytical and are not clearly independent biological samples. Allicin is reactive and can change during homogenization/extraction; source notes solvent-dependent degradation of products. Candidate held; Stage B checksum gate remains active.
